Capabilities beyond upstream are wz features, composed by Kconfig and SCE like any other

Owner 2026-10-30 supersedes the caveat above: wz is a framework, upstream is one preset

11.intent: Multi-layer testing strategy: byte-equivalence parity, wire replay, upstream interop, no-alloc guard, drift detection, fuzz.

11/11.1.intent: Cross-backend parity gate — every algorithm/codec with sce:test-vector runs on both backends and is byte-diffed; gate on merge.

11/11.2.intent: Wire replay tests — pcap captures from upstream zenoh peers replayed into generated stack with declared expected event sequence.

11/11.3.intent: Upstream interop CI — dockerized zenohd + AP node + MCU host-mode build (lwIP shim, renode/QEMU later) asserting full handshake + pub/sub roundtrip.

11/11.4.intent: MCU heap prohibition enforced as five layers — direct trap, linker wrap, libc pin, call-graph reachability, exception ban — not runtime trap alone.
rationale_bullets: Layer 1 direct trap: malloc/calloc/realloc/free stubs emit __builtin_trap on call.
Layer 2 linker --wrap: -Wl,--wrap on alloc symbols routes libc-internal indirect calls to traps.
Layer 3 libc pin: newlib-nano or picolibc tiny stdio prevents allocating printf path.
Layer 4 call-graph: post-link analyzer rejects any reach from out/mcu to deny-listed allocator.
Layer 5 exception ban: -fno-exceptions/-fno-rtti/-fno-unwind-tables blocks libstdc++ machinery.

11/11.5.intent: Drift gate: every emitted file carries source-hash + template-hash; sce-build verify recomputes and fails on mismatch; manual edits to out/ forbidden.
rationale_bullets: Per-file header carries source-hash + template-hash (sha256 over inputs and sce-build binary).
sce-build verify recomputes both hashes and fails the gate on mismatch (CI + pre-commit).
Fixed artifact set: out/{ap,mcu}, Cargo.toml, CMakeLists.txt, linker fragments, sce_sourcemap.json.
Manual edits to out/ forbidden: path is RFC or sce:extern; exceptions tracked with expiry date.
sce_sourcemap.json hash mismatch surfaces as traceability/sourcemap-source-hash-mismatch.

11/11.6.intent: Adversarial input fuzz testing on generated codec/parsers; deferred Phase D+ work; complements §11.1 cross-backend parity.

2/2.3.intent: MCU-class permanent constraints (no router, no aggregation, no heap, no scripting, no unbounded KeyExpr, no dynamic loading); AP unaffected.

2/2.4.intent: Six extensibility invariants: static-first, link-extensible, kinds-additive, library-not-monolith, platform gating, out/ SSoT.
rationale_bullets: Static-first, dynamic-opt-in: every MCU-static feature should admit an AP-dynamic variant.
Link drivers extensible: open set via target plugin, not closed enum.
Kinds additive: ForgeKind set grows; existing kinds remain stable across versions.
Generated code exports as library, not monolith: out/ap and out/mcu are library targets.
Platform gating only when physically necessary; keep pool/link/worker kinds platform-neutral.
out/ is SSoT-downstream: manual edits forbidden; new features land via SCE extensions.

3.intent: Four design invariants: zero-runtime abstraction, location transparency, strict SSoT, hardware-aware codegen.

3/3.1.intent: Zero-Runtime Abstraction — no vtables, no dynamic dispatch in the hot path; all bindings resolve at build time to direct calls (SCE AOT philosophy carried through).

3/3.2.intent: Location Transparency — SCXML uses logical identities; physical transport realization and addressing live in deploy.yaml; same SCXML deploys to AP or MCU.

3/3.3.intent: Strict SSoT — wire format / algorithms / FSMs defined once in SCXML+Forge; AP and MCU are descendants; cross-backend drift is a generator bug, not expected.

3/3.4.intent: Hardware-Aware Codegen — MCU code integrates with target SoC capabilities (SRAM placement, DMA pairing, alignment) declared via deploy.yaml; AP/MCU share no memory.

4.intent: Mapping of SCE existing capabilities, RFC-requested extensions, and watching-zenoh authoring scope.

4/4.2.intent: SCE extensions requested via RFC — new kinds (algorithm/link/buffer-pool/worker/bounded-collection), codec DSL, fragment pattern, C11 backend, no_std statechart, sce:extern, deploy fields.

4/4.3.intent: Project authoring scope — SCXML statecharts, Forge codec/algorithm/bounded-collection/link/pool/worker sources, deploy.yaml variants, runtime crates, optional API shim.

7/7.1.intent: AP backend stack — generated code on top of sce_core + sce_link_runtime_tokio + Rust std/bytes/tokio; tokio::spawn workers, mpsc channels, BytesMut pools.

7/7.2.intent: MCU stack — generated code over sce_forge_runtime_c + sce_link_runtime_lwip; cooperative tick scheduler with WCET budget; static pools + DMA descriptors.

7/7.3.intent: Shared runtime crates/headers — sce_core (AP only), sce_forge_runtime (Rust+C variants), sce_link_runtime_{tokio,lwip}, sce_intrinsics_runtime (whitelisted).

8.intent: Wire format layering: scouting/transport/network/zenoh/extensions; FSM, codec, link layers.

8/8.1.intent: Wire format stack layer diagram — Application -> Session FSM -> Network FSM -> Codec -> Link -> OS/HAL; bottom-up data flow on RX, top-down on TX.

8/8.2.intent: Session FSM sketch — Init/Scouting/Opening/Established/Closing path authored as session_unicast/multicast.scxml; full model lives in docs/session-fsm.md.

8/8.3.intent: Codec layer — one SCXML file per message type using RFC §5.B extensions (flags/vle/present-if/len-prefix/TLV); test vectors drive cross-backend parity.

8/8.4.intent: Link layer — kind=link SCXML files (UDP unicast/multicast/TCP/Serial/WS) with framer + RX-pool + backpressure declared; driver and address bound via deploy.yaml.

9.intent: Zero-copy: TX always zero-copy; RX happy path zero-copy; oversized/fragment stage-copy; pool placement; platform-aware link.

9/9.1.intent: TX path zero-copy — Codec encodes directly into pool slot, link send-from-slot, DMA reads via prebuilt descriptor; pool slot in DMA-coherent SRAM.

9/9.2.intent: RX happy path zero-copy — DMA writes pre-programmed RX slot; codec parses in place; event emitted with slot borrow; slot returned to freelist.

9/9.3.intent: Stage-copy RX path for oversized/multi-DMA — one copy DMA-slot to stage; build-time fragmentation analysis; stage_copy_policy warn/error/forbid per machine.

9/9.4.intent: Pool placement across .dtcm/.sram1/.flash regions; per-pool placement declared in kind source; memory regions in deploy.yaml; linker fragment ties them.

9/9.5.intent: Platform-aware link substrate: 5-row matrix (MCU bare_metal, linux+epoll, linux+io_uring, QNX, etc) sharing pool FSM.

intrinsics-runtime--symbol-surface.intent: Defines sce_intrinsics_runtime symbol surface (C11/Rust variants) for atomics/fences/cache/IRQ/RNG/HMAC/HW-sem.
inputs_bullets: RFC sec 5.I sce:extern whitelist — atomics, fences, cache maintenance, IRQ control
RFC sec 5.J.2 — statechart no_std HAL trait shape (ticks/wake/irq-save)
RFC sec 5.K target_plugin extension — per-SoC HMAC + HW semaphores out of core whitelist
session-fsm sec 2.7 G-SFM-5 — HMAC + RNG primitive ownership question (OQ-W15)
reassembly-fsm sec 6 — cache maintenance pinning (sec 5.E pool FSM call sites)
ARCHITECTURE sec 9.5 5-row matrix — same symbol set, different bodies per row
outputs_bullets: Categorized symbol table marking core whitelist vs target plugin per category
sec 5.J.2 statechart no_std HAL trait mapped onto these symbols
Cross-reference into RFC sec 5.I diagnostic list for authoring violation traceability
caveats_bullets: OQ-W14 (HW-sem standardization) and OQ-W15 (HMAC+RNG ownership) gate final shape.
Initial proposal: option 2 for HMAC (target plugin), option 1 for RNG (core whitelist).
Non-outputs: symbol body implementations, per-SoC HMAC accelerator binding.

intrinsics-runtime--symbol-surface/2-1-a.intent: Atomics core whitelist — per-width (u8-u64+usize) load/store/cas/fetch_* with explicit memory ordering encoded in the symbol name; no integer ordering parameter.

intrinsics-runtime--symbol-surface/2-2-f.intent: Fences core whitelist — atomic_fence_{acquire/release/acq_rel/seq_cst}, compiler_barrier (no runtime cost), dma_fence (DSB on ARMv7-M+, no-op on linux).

intrinsics-runtime--symbol-surface/2-3-c.intent: Cache maintenance core whitelist on MCU, no-op on AP linux (kernel-coherent); emitted only on §5.E pool lifecycle FSM edges; direct <sce:call> rejected.

intrinsics-runtime--symbol-surface/2-4-i.intent: IRQ control core whitelist (optional) — irq_save/irq_restore; only emitted for workers with sce:critical-section (RFC §5.D, Phase C+); MVP deploys do not use these.

intrinsics-runtime--symbol-surface/2-5-r.intent: RNG target plugin row (OQ-W15 (a) Q1 ratified Round 11: core whitelist rejected; sce_random_fill consumed by stateless_accept cookie HMAC key gen).

Impl multiplicity (HW TRNG / ADC+Yarrow / getrandom / arc4random) places RNG in plugin tier.
Fallback validated by SCE c13_beta_antiflood tests (baseline ∪ plugin lookup, 4570a389).

RNG WCET cleanly handled by canonical symbol with measured bound, no per-deploy redeclaration
HMAC HW-accelerator selection genuinely per-SoC (CRYP/SHA/SW fallback)
HMAC SW fallback authorable as algorithm kind (option 3 fallback path)
HMAC bounded blast radius — keeps whitelist small, contains crypto precedent

not viable, entropy generation is platform-coupled
adds 32-byte crypto, sets precedent for more crypto primitives
loses HW accelerator, ~10x CPU on STM32H7, tight WCET headroom

oq-w15-a--ratification-summary-for-sce-m.intent: Detailed counter-option matrix for the two decisions, expanding the trade-offs that §3 cites in summary form.

HMAC plugin (proposal): future crypto land by precedent; whitelist stays small
HMAC plugin (proposal): SoC-vendor crypto IP changes absorbed without RFC churn

HMAC core alt: faster Phase A on listener MCUs; precedent for crypto whitelist adds

reassembly-fsm--prose-sketch/1-framing-o.intent: Reassembly FSM between codec (Fragment) and network FSMs; chain key=(peer_zid, reliability) — two buffers per peer per upstream wire shape.
inputs_bullets: Chain key (peer_zid 16B, reliability 1bit); no priority, no sn_base in key
Wire: Fragment {sn:u64 VLE, payload:ZSlice, more bit, reliability bit}
FRAGMENT_FIRST/DROP exts patch-1+; legacy patch-0 infers first via empty+consecutive SN
Fragment classification: First / Continue / Final / Drop / unmatched-continue dropped at Router

reassembly-fsm--prose-sketch/10-next-ste.intent: Reassembly FSM unblocks Phase A SCXML authoring of sources/network/reassembly.scxml; deploy.yaml reassembly_pool block fully named; OQ-W22 closed.

reassembly-fsm--prose-sketch/2-1-hierarc.intent: ReassemblyDispatcher = Router dispatcher + N slot-FSM instances (N=slot_count, build-const); one-active-per-key. N identical slots via instantiation (Engines in pool), not orthogonal regions.
inputs_bullets: Router: Rust dispatcher (registry pattern) — routing-over-tables, not a state machine
Router map: chain-key→slot-index (bounded-collection<SlotEntry,N>); per-peer quota check
Slot: reassembly-protocol statechart, instantiated per slot as SCE Engine<ReassemblySlotPolicy>
Slot four states; real orthogonality is per-slot: memory-lifecycle ∥ reassembly-protocol FSM
<parallel> reserved for fixed distinct concerns, not N-identical slots (= instantiation)
Upstream divergence: shared bounded pool decoupled from peer count (vs upstream inline 2×peers)
Parity invariant: slot_count ≥ 2 × peer_table.capacity reproduces upstream no-exhaustion
MCU slot_count=4, AP=32 (OQ-W8); over-commits trade strict parity for memory cost
caveats_bullets: R311ij realized engine-free: <sce:action> + native more-bit guard, needs_script_engine=false
R311ij SN-consecutive not native-guardable -> dispatcher pre-classifies chunk vs ooo
R311ij FSM cross-compiles thumbv7em no_std; buffer = wz-side BoundedVec per slot

reassembly-fsm--prose-sketch/2-2-slot-st.intent: Slot four-state FSM: Empty → Receiving → Complete / TimedOut / Aborted (three terminals funnel back to Empty via slot release).
inputs_bullets: Empty: slot free, awaiting allocation from Router
Receiving: chain in progress; consecutive Continue allowed
Complete: Final received with consecutive SN
TimedOut: reassembly_timeout_ms expired
Aborted: 7 reasons (OOO/Drop/duplicate-First/oldest-wins/codec-error/unmatched/peer-drop)
Slot release transitions buffer-pool slot cpu-mut/cpu-ref → free (lifecycle FSM funnel)

reassembly-fsm--prose-sketch/2-3-router-.intent: Router = dispatcher (registry): routes Fragment.* to the chain-key's slot FSM instance; enforces per-peer quota; refuses second First on an open key (duplicate-first abort); not an SCXML region.

reassembly-fsm--prose-sketch/2-4-transit.intent: Eight detailed transitions across Slot states: Empty→Receiving (First), Receiving→Receiving (Continue), Final→Complete, plus 5 abort variants and Terminal→Empty release funnel.
outputs_bullets: §2.4.1 Empty→Receiving: Fragment.First admitted by Router (key not-active, quota OK, slot OK)
§2.4.2 Receiving→Receiving: Fragment.Continue with consecutive SN appends payload
§2.4.3 Receiving→Complete: Fragment.Final consecutive SN, emit message-complete event
§2.4.4 Receiving→Aborted: out-of-order Continue (non-consecutive SN, strict in-order)
§2.4.6 Receiving→Aborted: oldest-wins eviction by Router under pool pressure
§2.4.7 Receiving→Aborted: codec error on payload decode (§2.4.7a peer-drop via DROP ext)
§2.4.8 Terminal→Empty: slot release funnel; lifecycle FSM cpu-mut→free

reassembly-fsm--prose-sketch/2-5-out-of-.intent: Strict in-order policy (OQ-W21 closed): non-consecutive Continue aborts the chain (option 2 ratified); upstream consecutive-SN parity preserved.

reassembly-fsm--prose-sketch/2-6-mapping.intent: Mapping prose four-state Slot FSM (Empty/Receiving/Complete/TimedOut/Aborted) to RFC §5.M three-state high-level sketch (Idle/Active/Done) with terminal split.

reassembly-fsm--prose-sketch/3-tx-fragme.intent: TX fragmentation sibling FSM — chunks outbound NetworkMessage exceeding link MTU into Fragment.{First, Continue, Final} with consecutive SN.

reassembly-fsm--prose-sketch/4-timer-quo.intent: Reassembly timer / per-peer quota / pool config from deploy.yaml — reassembly_timeout_ms, per_peer_quota, slot_count, slot_size live under buffer_pools.reassembly_pool.
caveats_bullets: R311ij timeout = dispatcher worker-tick deadline-sweep, not an FSM <send delay> (SCE no <cancel>)
R311ij slots reused; sweep targets only the live slot, not stale (cf. RFC 815 GC)

reassembly-fsm--prose-sketch/5-trust-cla.intent: Trust-class interaction — reassembly forbidden on untrusted/session_arming links; established_session sibling instance receives reassembly bindings (OQ-W22 close).

Round 4520.decision_summary: A router now keeps what it declared to a face past the face's last interest, as upstream's broker keeps a face's local subscribers, queryables and tokens after an `Interest(Final)` and retracts each by the id it was declared under. The store dropped a face's record and its id counter with the face's last interest, so a client that kept the row of a subscriber it had been told was never told the subscriber went: its publisher's matching status stayed true for ever. Hosted macOS `C ABI` failed on this four runs in a row, where the undeclare reached the router before the next publisher's interest; on Linux the next interest usually came first and re-used id 1 by chance. A face's entry now goes only when it holds neither an interest nor a declaration, ids are not reused while a face may hold them, a reply declared for an aggregate interest stays one after the interest ends, and a C ABI router node's local face keeps its token bindings past its last subscriber.

Round 4526.decision_summary: Step 4a of the staged policy binding: a node's policies are chosen when it opens, from the `wz` member of its zenoh JSON5 document. The values come in layers, the build defaults, then a named profile (`wz/profile`, declared in `deploy/wz-config.toml` and generated into the build; one, `upstream`, every policy at upstream's behaviour), then the document's own `wz/policies`, each value recording the layer it came from. Every statement of every layer is validated before any is applied, so a configuration is never partly applied: one refusal refuses the document, and every refusal found is reported by name (a policy the build does not have, a value the policy does not have with the values it has, a value outside the build's domain naming the domain, a policy only the build decides, a value that is not a string, a member that is not an object, a profile the build does not have, a member stated twice, a member of `wz` the reader does not read, and `wz/limits`, refused as step 4b's). The zenoh config reader resolves the member into the node config; a zenoh-c open runs under it and a refused member fails the open as an invalid configuration (`Z_EINVAL`); the demo hands a `--config` file's snapshot down to its tuning and scouting sockets. A document with no `wz` member runs under the build defaults, as before. The pico and cooperative opens keep the build defaults until their config doors (step 5), and so does the Rust API, whose `Config` has no door for the member yet.

What TLS 1.2 sends in the clear is read in the clear; TLS 1.3's certificate and its alerts after the ServerHello are read out of the records a key log opened, so without one a TLS 1.3 refusal is undecided with no alert, and the document says so. PIN RE-DECLARED (R2394): this entry's `source` field still reads "zenoh downsampling plugin" and the inventory mutate API has no setter for it, so the pin is declared here instead -- everything below is measured against zenoh 1.10.0, this tree's pin, at `zenoh/src/net/routing/interceptor/downsampling.rs` @ `fn is_msg_filtered` and `commons/zenoh-config/src/lib.rs` @ `pub enum DataMessage`. THE RE-MEASUREMENT REFUTED THE PREVIOUS GRADE, which is why this atom was worth picking. The entry graded COMPLETE against 1.5.0 with the `messages` selector ported as a three-variant DownsamplingMessage {Push, Query, Reply}, and wz carried a doc comment asserting that the coarseness was upstream's -- that the downsampling filter dispatched one kind per NETWORK body while the sibling low-pass matched the inner body, so "the asymmetry is upstream's, and porting each faithfully reproduces it". At the pin that sentence is FALSE. The pin's filter destructures the push body and reads Put and Del through SEPARATE selector bits (`zenoh/src/net/routing/interceptor/downsampling.rs` @ `PushBody::Del(_) => self.delete`), and the downsampling and low-pass interceptors select over the SAME four-variant config enum (`commons/zenoh-config/src/lib.rs` @ `pub enum DataMessage`), which that enum's own doc comment names as shared by downsampling, low-pass and the SHM optimization. There is no push-arm asymmetry left to port, and the three-variant mirror could not express "rate-limit the deletes and leave the puts alone", which the pin can. A COMPLETE grade was therefore recording a divergence as a port -- not merely stale, wrong about the upstream this tree exists to replace. WHAT R2394 BUILT, so the grade is true at the pin rather than re-tagged: DownsamplingMessage is the pin's four kinds (Put, Delete, Query, Reply) and the classifier resolves a push on its BODY (crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/interceptor/downsampling.rs, `fn message_kinds`). The request and response arms stay body-BLIND, which the same re-measurement CONFIRMED is still upstream's shape -- a Put or Del routed as a Request is a Query to the pin's filter and to wz -- so that half of the ported asymmetry survives and is now recorded as measured rather than assumed. A FOURTH DELIBERATE DIVERGENCE, in the same direction as the three below: wz's generated push codec has a `Default` arm the pin's two-variant PushBody has no counterpart for, reached by any body tag but put/del, so a remote peer can put one on the wire. Answering "no kind" would leave it UNGOVERNED -- a rate limit evaded by mislabelling a body -- so an unnameable push body is governed whenever the rule names Put or Del. That is this module's stated fail-CLOSED direction for an indeterminate subject, applied to an indeterminate KIND. THREE DAMAGES BOUND THE BUILD, each redding exactly one test and each measured rather than asserted: collapsing the classifier's two push arms reds message_kind_classifies_the_bodies_zenoh_throttles; making Put and Delete interchangeable inside the selector filter reds a_rule_on_puts_leaves_deletes_alone_on_the_same_keyexpr; making an unnameable body resolve to no kind reds an_indeterminate_push_body_is_governed_by_either_data_kind. The third test earned that shape from a GREEN control probe: written against admit_at with a two-kind slice it passed under its own damage, because nothing bound the classifier arm that produces the slice, so it drives a real unknown-tag push now. R311y452 closed four residuals and R311y453 the fifth, and all five REMAIN closed at the pin: the per-rule messages selector; body-level kind dispatch; the per-rule flows selector, with for_flow installing NO interceptor on an ungoverned flow (`zenoh/src/net/routing/interceptor/downsampling.rs` @ `fn new_transport_unicast`); the rate as upstream's FREQUENCY in Hertz through the interval_from_freq SSOT (`zenoh/src/net/routing/interceptor/downsampling.rs` @ `const NANOS_PER_SEC`), including the freq == 0.0 DROP-ALL edge that drops even the first message; and the interfaces / link_protocols SUBJECT scoping (`commons/zenoh-config/src/lib.rs` @ `pub struct DownsamplingItemConf`), resolved once at link open from the driver that owns the socket (wz-session-core link.rs LinkSubject; wz-runtime-tokio link_interfaces.rs). THREE DELIBERATE IMPROVEMENTS ON UPSTREAM, each still a defect at the pin that wz does not reproduce: (1) zenoh caches the host interface table in a process-lifetime lazy_static so a NIC appearing later is invisible for the life of the process, while wz calls getifaddrs live; (2) zenoh maps a FAILED interface lookup to the same empty vec it uses for a link genuinely on no NIC, while wz is three-state -- resolved names, a definite non-match, could-not-determine; (3) zenoh's two subject axes disagree with each other, interfaces requiring EVERY link to match and SKIPPING the check on a get_links error while link_protocols requires ANY and installs nothing on a get_auth_ids error, whereas wz applies ONE policy to both -- ANY, and fail-CLOSED on an indeterminate subject, the conservative direction because all three 5.16 interceptors are restrictive when they apply. CROSS-IMPL PROVEN R311y452 + R311y453: a real zenoh-pico z_pub burst of 3 Puts at its own 1 Hz cadence is admitted exactly ONCE by a governing rule (crates/wz-integration-tests/tests/wz_peer_downsampling_pico_interop.rs), and the SUBJECT axis is proven by A/B against the same burst -- a rule narrowed to the protocol pico dials (tcp) throttles while the identical rule narrowed to vsock is inert, and a rule narrowed to lo throttles the accepted loopback link while one narrowed to an absent NIC is inert (crates/wz-integration-tests/tests/wz_peer_subject_scoping_pico_interop.rs). Both run in run-ci Layer E6, hosted. UPDATE (R3069) -- A DELIVERY A SESSION MAKES TO ITSELF RUNS INSIDE THE CALL THAT CAUSES IT, ON THE CALLING THREAD, AS ZENOH-C RUNS IT; THE ATOM STAYS PARTIAL. Item (3) of the clause above that says FOUND, NOT FIXED is superseded. MEASURED FIRST, with one C program linked to each library, pausing after every operation so the ORDER and not a race is what is compared: on the real library a put whose subscriber is in the same session, a publisher's put, a delete, a put made from inside a callback, a get against a queryable of the same session (the query, its reply, the reply's callback and the final), a get made from inside a callback and a subscriber declared from inside one all run every callback BEFORE the call returns and on the calling thread, and a put made from inside a callback runs the inner callback between the outer one's first and last event. wz staged each of them for its drive thread, and every one came out after the call returned, on another thread. THE PREMISE THAT HELD THAT WAS WZ'S, NOT UPSTREAM'S: R311y554 kept every C callback on one thread so that `unsafe impl Sync` on the closure wrappers read as sound, and zenoh-c's own closure types carry the same impl with no promise about the calling thread; the wrappers only read their fields, and what the C function does with its context is the program's. A program that puts and then reads what its callback set read the old value, and one that printed from both printed in the other order. BUILT. Which thread drains the node's own plane is the calling ABI's choice, a field of the resources every session of a node is given (`crates/wz-capi-core/src/faces.rs` @ `pub local_delivery: LocalDeliveryDrain,`): this ABI's open says `Caller` (`crates/wz-capi-c/src/session.rs` @ `local_delivery: LocalDeliveryDrain::Caller,`) and zenoh-pico's keeps `DriveTask`, because its callbacks are an executor's (`crates/wz-capi-pico/src/session.rs` @ `local_delivery: wz_runtime_tokio::session::LocalDeliveryDrain::DriveTask,`). A face session keeps `DriveTask` for both: its loopback is `Locality::Remote`, so it has no same-session delivery of its own. The deferred-fire queue was built for several drainers (a callback that finds another mid-fire backlogs its call and nothing is lost), so the drive thread draining what a declaration left behind beside a caller draining its own put is a case it already handles. The comments that stated the single-thread premise were rewritten where they would now be false (the closure wrappers' in `crates/wz-capi-c/src/sub.rs` and the modules beside it, and the registry's). ONE REGRESSION WAS MEASURED AND FIXED IN THE SAME ROUND: a chunk put to a local subscriber read `SHM (IMMUT)` where the real library's reads `SHM (MUT)`, because the put still held its own reference while the callback ran inside it, where before it had dropped it by the time the drive thread ran the callback (`zenoh_c_shm_local_delivery_twice_and_diff.rs` went red the first time the whole set ran against the change). Of the 561 exported functions the audit's scan parsed (the macro-generated handle families are not in it), the only ones whose body is a constant and that pico does not also stub are those four, so this is the one runtime-lifecycle seam left and not the first of many. NOT DONE BY THIS: hosted Layers E and E5 at HEAD are unread; the legs ran on one machine; the connectivity plane was compared on the wire for TCP and a peer only, and the constants of the other link kinds are pinned against pico's source and not observed; a multicast transport and a session with several wire faces were not exercised.

CORRECTION (R2992) -- THE SESSION'S READ TASK, WHICH THE LINE ABOVE NAMED AS THE LAST LIVE RESIDUAL, IS BUILT, AND BUILDING IT FOUND A SECOND DEFECT IN ITS OWN FIRST CUT. THE ATOM IS COMPLETE, WITH THE NON-CLAIMS BELOW.

WHAT IS BUILT. `z_open` reads `auto_start_read_task` (`crates/wz-capi-pico/src/session.rs` @ `let start_read_task = options.is_null() || (*options).auto_start_read_task;`), as pico starts its executor only when it is set (`vendor/zenoh-pico/src/api/api.c` @ `if (opts.auto_start_read_task) {`). One gate (`crates/wz-capi-core/src/drive.rs` @ `pub struct ReadGate {`) stands in front of the session's single top-level drive future (`crates/wz-capi-core/src/drive.rs` @ `struct Pausable<F> {`): while the task is stopped that future is not polled, which is a stopped executor -- nothing is read, no keep-alive is sent, no lease is checked, nobody is accepted, and what arrives waits in the socket. The open itself is never gated, because pico connects and binds inside `z_open` before any executor could run. A face waits at the gate right after its open and the listen role before its accept loop, so frames already in the socket when `z_open` returns are not read in the poll that announced it. `zp_start_read_task`, `zp_stop_read_task` and `zp_read_task_is_running` read and move the gate, and `zp_lease_task_is_running` answers the same state as pico's does; the lease start and stop stay `Z_OK` constants because pico's are (`vendor/zenoh-pico/src/api/api.c` @ `z_result_t zp_start_lease_task(z_loaned_session_t *zs, const zp_task_lease_options_t *options) {`). A `z_put` and a `z_close` of a stopped session still run, since the writers are tasks of their own, as pico writes on the caller's thread.

THE SECOND DEFECT, FOUND BY ASKING WHAT A STOP PROMISES RATHER THAN WHAT IT DOES. The first cut answered `Z_OK` at once to a stop and to a start made anywhere. pico's stop suspends its executor and joins the executor's thread, so when it returns no callback is running and none will (`vendor/zenoh-pico/src/runtime/background_executor.c` @ `_Z_SET_IF_OK(ret, _z_task_join(&task_to_join));`), and a stop or a start made on that thread, which is where every callback runs, is refused with `_Z_ERR_INVALID` and does nothing (`vendor/zenoh-pico/src/runtime/background_executor.c` @ `return _Z_ERR_INVALID;  // suspend cannot be called from executor thread`). Two differential legs were written FIRST against the real library and run against the first cut, and they were red on exactly those two lines: a stop made while a callback was in flight returned with `no-callback-running-after-stop=0` and `nothing-delivered-after-stop=0` where pico prints 1 and 1, and a stop and a start from inside a callback printed `rc=0 running=0` and `rc=0 running=1` where pico prints `rc=-75 running=1` twice. A stop now wakes the drive thread and waits until it has parked, and a call made on the drive thread gets `crates/wz-capi-core/src/drive.rs` @ `pub struct CalledFromReadTask;` back, which `zp_stop_read_task` (`crates/wz-capi-pico/src/session.rs` @ `pub unsafe extern "C" fn zp_stop_read_task(zs: *mut z_loaned_session_t) -> ZResult {`) maps to pico's code.

MEASURED against the real libzenohpico by six compile-twice legs (`crates/wz-integration-tests/tests/pico_read_task_twice_and_diff.rs` @ `fn stopping_the_read_task_waits_for_the_callback_in_flight_and_holds_the_rest() {`), each with its reference arm asserted to carry the behaviour before the two arms are compared: (1) a LISTENING session opened without the task, where a demo dials in and nothing is accepted, the declared subscriber gets all five of its Puts after a start, a stop holds a SECOND demo dialling in, a put from the stopped session reaches its peer, a restart delivers the second five, and closing a stopped session returns; (2) the same with the task running from the open, the negative arm that a build which held every session back cannot pass; (3) a session that DIALS a listening demo without the task, which is the usual shape of the flag; (4) that dial through a proxy that delivers the demo's OPEN ack and its whole burst in one write, so the five Puts are in the socket before `z_open` returns and before the subscriber exists; (5) a stop while a 300 ms callback runs; (6) a stop and a start from inside a callback.

CONTROLS, each applied alone to committed source: the gate never armed (red in the held legs, green in the running one); the top-level future never parked (red in the listening and running legs, green in the dialled one); the close waking the gate only after the join (the close of a stopped session never returns, so every leg that closes stopped is red); the face not waiting after its open (red in both dialled legs, and ONLY the proxy leg is deterministic: the plain dialled leg was green in one run of the control and red in the next, because the demo's first Put arrives a few milliseconds after its OPEN ack, which is why the proxy leg exists); and, in the gate's unit tests, the stop not waking the drive thread, the drive never acknowledging its park, the refusal on the drive thread removed and the stop not waiting, each red in exactly the one test written for it. THE FIRST RUN OF THE FACE CONTROL CAME BACK GREEN, against three legs, and is reported rather than dropped: the plain dialled leg cannot reach the window in which a face reads in the poll that announced its open. A first build of the close control did not compile (its method became dead code) and its run was void; it was repeated.

WHAT CLOSES THE ATOM. The residual list this atom carried was re-derived from the tree rather than read off the prose above: (a) the real `libzenohpico.so` defines 774 public `z_`, `zp_` and `ze_` symbols and wz's cdylib defines 776 of them, none missing (`crates/wz-integration-tests/tests/pico_abi_symbol_census.rs` @ `fn defined_dynamic_symbols(path: &Path) -> BTreeSet<String> {`); (b) of the 561 exported functions a scan of the crate's source parses, the 15 whose body is a constant are default constructors of pico's own enums and structs, a random byte, and four that pico stubs the same way -- the two lease-task functions and `z_link_priorities` and `z_link_reliability` (`vendor/zenoh-pico/src/api/api.c` @ `bool z_link_priorities(const z_loaned_link_t *link, uint8_t *min_out, uint8_t *max_out) {`); (c) the options gate (`scripts/lib/pico_option_field_reader_gate.py` @ `UNREAD_WITH_REASON = {`) lists eleven option fields that nothing reads, each with the reason, and `auto_start_read_task` is no longer one of them.

NOT CLAIMED, and named so that it is not read into the grade: hosted Layers E and E5 at HEAD are unread by this round and the legs ran on one machine. The read task was observed on TCP unicast only -- in a listening session, in a client dialling one endpoint, and through the proxy -- and not in a peer session dialling several endpoints or over a multicast transport, where the same gate is wired (each face waits at it) but was not observed. That a stopped session sends no keep-alive and checks no lease holds by construction, since its drive future is not polled, and was not watched on the wire; a stop lasting longer than a lease was not exercised. A stop takes effect when the drive future next yields and not between two frames, so frames already buffered may be delivered while a stop is in progress; after it returns none is, which is the promise pico makes and the one the legs check. The `task_attributes` option of the task functions has no observable effect and is ignored, and the build of pico without multi-threading (`zp_read`, `zp_send_keep_alive`) is a different configuration that this atom never measured.

api-compat-rust.source: zenoh 1.10.2 (owner decision 2026-10-22; the surface scripts/lib/rust_api_surface.py holds)
api-compat-rust.reason: PARTIAL: the Rust public API of the pinned zenoh family as a drop-in over wz, so a Rust user replaces zenoh by one `[patch.crates-io]` entry per crate and every crate of the graph, an ecosystem crate included, meets the same types. THE UNIT OF REPLACEMENT IS A CRATE UNDER UPSTREAM'S PACKAGE NAME, not a dependency line (owner decision 2026-10-24, refining the 2026-10-22 decision and docs/build-configuration.md C13): measured, a `[patch]` whose package is named otherwise is not used by Cargo and the graph keeps upstream's crate, so an ecosystem crate that imports `zenoh_core` meets a second, different one, and a patch under the same name unifies them. The family is therefore every crate the public API names (a reexport line of the surface names its origin) and the ecosystem imports, each held to its own upstream surface (`scripts/lib/rust_api_surface.py` @ `MEMBERS: tuple[Member, ...] = (`) and to upstream's behaviour by differential tests (Layer E18). BUILT: zenoh-result, complete (`crates/wz-zenoh-result/Cargo.toml` @ `name = "zenoh-result"`): the whole of its surface, no line missing and none extra, six differential tests against upstream's crate (two injected faults each turned exactly the test that owns it red), and the swap proved on a graph in which upstream's own `zenoh-keyexpr` raises an error that is the `ZError` of the patched crate (`conformance/patch-scenario/tests/one_zenoh_result.rs` @ `fn an_upstream_crates_error_is_the_zerror_of_the_patched_crate() {`), with the same graph unpatched as the control, where the downcast answers nothing because the graph holds two. Also BUILT: zenoh-runtime, complete, the one crate of the family that holds PROCESS-GLOBAL state (one pool of tokio runtimes, one per role, in a static), which is why it is a member and not a detail of zenoh-core: Cargo keeps one crate per package name, so one pool per process holds only while every crate meets this one. It is written by hand where upstream generates its configuration with two derive macros, its surface equals upstream's, and four differential tests run both crates as children under the same `ZENOH_RUNTIME` (the pool is configured once per process) and hold what each read, and which thread served each role after a handover, equal; two injected faults, a changed default thread count and a configuration that no longer refuses an unknown role, turned exactly their tests red. Also BUILT: zenoh-core, complete (`crates/wz-zenoh-core/Cargo.toml` @ `name = "zenoh-core"`): the resolve traits `Resolvable`, `Wait` and `Resolve` that every builder of `zenoh` and of `zenoh-ext` implements, `ResolveClosure` and `ResolveFuture` (whose `wait` blocks on the application runtime of zenoh-runtime), and the helper macros, its surface equal to upstream's line for line and six differential tests that expand every macro once per crate in a module naming that crate's own zenoh-result; two injected faults, a swapped `zcondfeat!` arm and a wait that no longer goes through the application runtime, turned three of the six red. Also BUILT, complete, in four slices: zenoh-keyexpr (`crates/wz-zenoh-keyexpr/Cargo.toml` @ `name = "zenoh-keyexpr"`), the key expression types `keyexpr`, `nonwild_keyexpr`, `OwnedKeyExpr`, `OwnedNonWildKeyExpr` and `Chunks`, canonization, the two relations and the generator, and, in the second slice, the key expression formats (`KeFormat`, `OwnedKeFormat`, the formatter, `Parsed` and the macro support), 356 of the 356 default lines and 368 of the 368 unstable ones, none missing and none extra: the algorithms are written from the language's definition and not transcribed, and `conformance/differential/tests/zenoh_keyexpr.rs` @ `fn both_crates_judge_every_short_string_alike_and_report_the_same_fault() {` holds them to upstream's over every string of a seven-letter alphabet up to length 7 (fault, message and error number alike) and every pair of the valid key expressions up to length 6 for intersection, inclusion and relation; it found two upstream faults it does not copy, a canonizer that folds only part of a run of three `$*` and one that panics on 663 short malformed strings, each pinned as a class wz answers by the definition; the format differential test compares about 480 thousand parses of 552 key expressions against 1,999 formats and found three more faults of upstream's that wz does not copy: a spec with a default (`${id:pattern#default}`) has its pattern cut wrong because the offset of the `#` is stored relative to the pattern and read as absolute, so every such format panics or is refused, and a format ending in `$` and a format with no spec at all panic. The third slice is the key expression trees (`crates/wz-zenoh-keyexpr/src/keyexpr_tree.rs` @ `pub mod box_tree;`): `KeBoxTree`, the node and tree traits, the three children providers and the iterators. The three relational iterators are one walk with one test per relation, and the children to visit are chosen by a rule derived from the language: a node without a `**` chunk can have a matching descendant only if it intersects a head of the query, and a node with one is always entered, because `**` matches no verbatim chunk and may match fewer chunks than the node has (a first version tested `<node>/**` and lost `**/@a` under `**`, which the generated-tree test found). The fourth slice is the tree whose nodes are shared (`crates/wz-zenoh-keyexpr/src/keyexpr_tree/arc_tree.rs` @ `pub struct KeArcTree<`): `KeArcTree`, its node, its token and the iterators that pair each node with the token, over `token-cell` as upstream's is. plugin-abi-compat.reason: FOUNDATIONAL: REALIZED R311y492 inside plugin-dynamic-loading, with no separate cfg toggle. R311y256 deprecated this atom ON THE CONDITION that dynamic loading was never built, in its own words: the four exist only to SERVE dynamic loading, so if that is ever built they return with it. It was built, so this returns -- deprecated -> reserved rather than -> active, because A3's invariant is active <=> at least one cfg(feature=..) site and this has none of its own. Realization: plugin-manager = PluginRegistry (BTreeMap-ordered so the admin reply order is deterministic); plugin-host-trait = wz_plugin_abi::PluginVTable, C function pointers rather than a Rust trait because Rust has no stable ABI across a dlopen boundary; plugin-lifecycle = Declared->Loaded in PluginRegistry::load plus Loaded->Started in DynamicPlugin::start, the first step existing precisely BECAUSE dlopen can fail; plugin-abi-compat = PluginEntry::compatibility, checking abi_major equality, abi_minor <= host, and vtable size+align -- the last catching a stale rebuild at an unchanged declared ABI. All four ride the single plugin-dynamic-loading cargo key: they are not independently selectable, and a registry with nothing loadable has no behaviour of its own. The ABI gate is bound by 5 unit tests in wz-plugin-abi; none of the four is claimed on the pico transcript, which would be per-compiled-feature claiming.

UPDATE (R3159-R3169) -- THE TRANSMIT HALF (SECTION 9.1) IS BUILT ON BOTH PROFILES, IN THE FORM THE LINK LENDS THE BUFFER, AND THE MCU RECEIVE SIDE (SECTION 9.2) IS HALF BUILT; THE GRADE STAYS PARTIAL AND THE EARLIER CLAUSES THAT SAY THE TRANSMIT PATH IS UNTOUCHED ARE FALSE. Measured against the code, the session cannot own the outbound buffer: the AP stream driver builds a second framed vector and hands it to its writer task by ownership, a multilink session has one link per pool, and only the link knows what its DMA domain needs in front of the payload. So the LINK LENDS and the session encodes. The seam is four defaulted methods on the link driver (acquire a slot with the headroom the link wants, name its storage, send it, abort it), a lease that is a buffer over the lent slot and gives it back if dropped unsent, and an outbound buffer trait that every encoder writes to, so a heap vector and a fixed slot are the same to the codec. The session's immediate and lowlatency send paths try a lease before the heap encode and fall back to the heap, with the sequence number already minted, when the link lends nothing, has no free slot, the encode overflows the slot, or the frame needs fragmenting; the wire is byte for byte the heap path's, witnessed against it. The reconnect swap seams forward the lend and remember which link lent each slot, so a swap in the middle of an encode sends and aborts on the link that lent it. ON THE AP the stream driver lends a vector with the framing prefix room in front of it, writes the prefix in place and enqueues the filled vector by ownership, and the writer task returns each buffer it has written to a small bounded pool (four buffers of at most 16 KiB) that the next lend draws from: two allocations and a copy per frame become none in steady state, witnessed by six frames through the real writer task leaving one buffer, with the pool read directly because a freed buffer's address is what the allocator hands the next request and so proves nothing. ON THE MCU the transmit chain is cut at all three copies that followed the encoder: the Ethernet MAC seam gains a gather transmit and a completion report, the CYT4BF MAC chains one descriptor per piece with the vendor driver's own protocol (read from its reference source) and reports a frame done only when the controller has finished reading it, the lwIP shim holds a reference on the pbuf chain and hands its pieces to the MAC in place, and the lwIP link driver lends the payload of a transport-layer pbuf so the session encodes straight into the datagram; a real pbuf chain whose payload piece is the caller's own memory reaches the MAC at that address with its reference count read as one. The RECEIVE side of the same MAC is cut at the first two of its three copies: the MAC lends a received frame where the controller wrote it and withholds that buffer from the controller until it is returned, the shim wraps it in a custom pbuf that points at it so lwIP reads it in place, and the buffer goes back to the MAC when lwIP frees the pbuf, which for a fragment parked in reassembly is long after the input call returned; the witness is a real lwIP stack receiving a datagram, an ARP reply and a two-fragment datagram through lent frames, each buffer coming back exactly once. Each layer has a red-first break that turns exactly its tests red, and the C and Rust compile for a Cortex-M target with the real lwIP sources. WHAT THIS DOES NOT RETIRE, each re-measured: (1) the generated pool's DMA transmit edges (arm for transmit, start transmit, transmit complete) still have no caller, the acquire-for-encode edge being used only by the receive-side staging, because the lent slot is the driver's own memory and the MAC ring and the pbuf reference count play the part those edges were declared for, so the pool lifecycle is not what governs a transmit buffer on any profile; (2) the AP writer queue's item is still an owned vector and not a pool slot, so an AP transmit buffer is not under the generated pool's lifecycle either, and a burst past the four spare buffers, or a frame past 16 KiB, still allocates; giving the queue a pool handle reaches the serial pipeline; (3) the batching path stages frames in a vector held across calls and flushes it through the byte door, so lending at flush would copy once into a slot where it now copies once into a vector, and the gain needs the stage buffer itself to be the slot, held across calls, a design decision about slots occupied for a batch window; (4) the MCU RECEIVE side still copies the datagram out of lwIP into an owned slot in the socket's receive callback, and the descriptor-ring walk that would bind the generated pool's receive arms to a MAC still has no MAC bound to it, because the MAC's receive buffers are its own ring and not pool slots; (5) there is NO HARDWARE witness: the controller model is written from the same documents as the driver, and the board's cache clean is a no-op that assumes the area is non-cacheable, which the pbufs in lwIP's own heap may not be. NOT MEASURED: the hosted verdict of these pushes, the footprint and stack lines of the QEMU lane with the new driver in it, and a run on the kit.

UPDATE (R3170-R3171) -- THE TRANSMIT SEAM IS A FEATURE, BECAUSE ITS FIRST HOSTED MEASUREMENT FOUND IT COSTING AN IMAGE THAT NEVER USES IT; THE GRADE STAYS PARTIAL. The footprint the paragraph above left unmeasured was read hosted and was red: the MCU multicast image grew 1456 bytes of ROM (thumbv7m 64172 to 65652) over the buffer seam, for a seam it never uses. A per-symbol diff names it: the payload encoders write through a fallible dyn TxBuf sink, which keeps the codec's error branch after every write, where a vector's push cannot fail and that branch folds away. The seam is now a feature of the session crate, transport-tx-lend, off by default, which both compiles the lend attempt and chooses the encoders' buffer type (the vector itself, or dyn TxBuf). A sink merely generic over the buffer would not have recovered the bytes: the link a session writes to is a trait object, so the lend attempt stays reachable and both instantiations stay linked, and only the composition can say that a slot is never lent. The AP runtime, the unicast MCU acceptor, the MCU admin node and the Zephyr admin node's lwIP backend turn it on; the multicast image does not, and the dependency graph shows the feature on the acceptor and off on the multicast image. Measured with the lane's own build: the multicast image 64344 (thumbv7m) and 64132 (thumbv7em-hf), 1308 and 1312 below the regression and 172 above the last tree before the seam, a difference no per-symbol diff has attributed; the acceptor's three QEMU boots pass, the admin node builds, the lwIP shell's 24 leg tests pass with the lend on through a dev-dependency, and the AP's session-level lend tests pass. WHAT THIS DOES NOT SETTLE: an image that links the lwIP shell and omits the feature does not fail, it silently stops lending and sends the heap frame (correct bytes, one copy more), and nothing in the tree fails on that omission; the Zephyr admin node's lend is a build-time claim that was not built on this host.

UPDATE (R3305) -- THE ATOM IS COMPLETE: EVERY CLAUSE THE EARLIER GRADE NAMED IS BUILT AND WITNESSED, ON THE AP AND ON THE MCU, AND THE TWO POOL IMAGES RAN ON SILICON. READ THE PARAGRAPHS ABOVE AS THE HISTORY OF THE GRADE: each WHAT IS LEFT, STILL PARTIAL, WHAT KEEPS THIS PARTIAL and WHAT THIS DOES NOT RETIRE clause in them was true at its round and is answered here clause by clause, re-measured against the tree and the ledger before it was written down. The grade follows the owner's scope decision of 2026-10-10, that all five clauses of the R3159-R3169 update be built and witnessed and none be narrowed away.
(1) THE GENERATED POOL'S DMA TRANSMIT EDGES HAVE CALLERS ON BOTH PROFILES. On the AP the link's transmit pool walks a slot through acquire, arm, start, complete and un-arm (`crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/link_tx_pool.rs` @ `slot.link_arm_tx(self)`, and `crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/link_tx_pool.rs` @ `unsafe { self.tx_complete(idx) }`). On the MCU the lwIP link owns a generated 8 x 1536 transmit pool, off by default behind its tx-pool feature and born with its consumer: a lent payload is a slot laid out as a custom pbuf, so lwIP writes its headers into the slot, and the slot walks armed, started, complete or un-armed (`crates/wz-link-lwip/src/tx_pool.rs` @ `if unsafe { pool.tx_complete(idx) } {`). Measured while building it (R3218): the Zephyr image's MAC wrapper forwarded only transmit and receive, so the image had never gathered a frame before, and the board's cache clean is a no-op, so the MAC now reads in place only memory its board declares readable (`crates/wz-eth-mac-cyt4bf/src/lib.rs` @ `fn reads_in_place(&self, ptr: *const u8, len: usize) -> bool;`); a lent heap pbuf is copied into the ring instead.
(2) THE AP WRITER QUEUE'S ITEM IS A POOL SLOT, NOT A VECTOR (R3239, R3240, R3264). A stream or serial link's writer queue owns its own generated transmit pool, 16 x 65600 (`crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/lib.rs` @ `pub mod session_tx_pool_ap {`), the item is a handle that walks the pool's transmit arms, frames pack back to back in a lane's newest slot, and a dry pool is back-pressure and never an allocation; the burst that used to allocate one buffer per frame past four now allocates nothing (`crates/wz-runtime-tokio/tests/stream_tx_pool_allocations.rs` @ `async fn a_burst_of_lent_frames_past_four_buffers_allocates_nothing() {`). A datagram link has its own small-class pool, a multicast push offers the queue a lend and encodes the datagram into the slot (`crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/multicast_pipeline.rs` @ `fn enqueue_lent(`, witnessed by `crates/wz-runtime-tokio/tests/datagram_tx_pool_allocations.rs` @ `fn a_steady_state_of_pooled_multicast_pushes_allocates_nothing() {`), and the websocket link frames the message in its slot, header and client mask included, because the 0.29 bump alone still left tungstenite copying the payload (`crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/ws_pipeline.rs` @ `pub fn frame_in_place(`, witnessed by `crates/wz-runtime-tokio/tests/datagram_tx_pool_allocations.rs` @ `fn the_frame_is_made_in_the_slot_the_message_was_encoded_into() {`). A spinning test thread found on the way was a product bug, not a test one: the outbound wait asked whether ANY class had a slot, so a frame only the large class holds spun at full CPU, and it now asks for the frame's own class. COUNTED, NOT HIDDEN: a multicast frame past the group's batch is still fragmented from the heap (5 allocations per 5000-byte push) and a multicast item's builder allocates 3 per item before the push; the suite counts both so neither can grow unseen. The serial framer's COBS stuffer allocates inside the SCE-generated emit, which is the emit's and not this atom's, and a test pins it.
(3) THE BATCHING STAGE IS A SLOT (R3238). A batch frame opens in a slot the conduit's link lends, is held across the window's calls as a pointer-free handle recorded on the lending link (`crates/wz-session-core/src/tx_lease.rs` @ `pub struct HeldSlot {`), takes each message straight into the slot with rollback on overflow, and its flush sends the slot, so a flush copies nothing; a dry pool or a link that lends nothing stages on the heap and counts it (`crates/wz-session-core/src/session_actions.rs` @ `pub fn batch_lend_counts(&self) -> BatchLendCounts {`). Occupancy is one slot per conduit, not one per window, because conduits stage independently.
(4) THE RECEIVE SIDE IS POOL-ROUTED ON BOTH PROFILES. On the AP the UDP receive (dial, accept demux, group and scouting reads) draws from the node's receive pool (`crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/link_rx_datagram.rs` @ `pub async fn recv_frame(socket: &UdpSocket)`, witnessed by `crates/wz-runtime-tokio/tests/datagram_rx_pool_allocations.rs` @ `fn every_path_delivers_what_the_copying_path_reads() {`), the stream links having been routed since R2742. On the MCU the CYT4BF MAC arms its receive descriptors with slots of a receive pool, lends a received frame to lwIP in the slot the controller wrote it into, and the session loop dispatches a lent datagram where the controller wrote it (rx-in-place; R3250). A fragment on that path is staged once into its slot of a reassembly arena the session owns over the generated table, its head read in place, and a completed message read in the slot record by record (`crates/wz-runtime-coop/src/reassembly_rx.rs` @ `pub struct ReassemblyArena {`, the observer handed `crates/wz-session-core/src/driver_loop.rs` @ `pub struct InPlaceFragment<'a> {`, witnessed by `crates/wz-session-lwip/tests/rx_frame_allocations.rs` @ `fn a_fragmented_message_is_staged_once_and_read_in_its_slot() {`); that fragment path is witnessed on the host and not on the kit, because the receive-pool image does not turn reassembly on.
(5) THE TRANSMIT LEND IS EXPLICIT, AND A PROFILE CAN FORBID THE HEAP (S3, S4, S9). Under tx-lend-only a refused lend is an explicit outcome and the frame is never built on the heap: `crates/wz-session-core/src/link.rs` @ `pub enum LinkSendOutcome {` carries a drop cause for a link that lent no slot, so the R3171 caveat that an image omitting the seam silently sends the heap frame no longer holds for the profile that selects it. The fixed-memory images (the unicast acceptor, the lwIP admin node, the Zephyr admin node and the multicast image) are held to a link with no allocator by the gate at `scripts/lib/no_allocator_link_gate.py` @ `IMAGES: dict[str, Image] = {`, whose mutant check turns it red when the allocator is named.
(6) HARDWARE, WHICH CLAUSE (5) OF R3159-R3169 SAID DID NOT EXIST. Both pool images were flashed to the T2G kit with the CM0+ launcher and judged by the verdict program from the boot's console, the onboard files and a host capture (Round 3270; the owner's permission for hardware writes, 2026-10-10 and 2026-10-11), and every step ended OK. TRANSMIT, HW.26 to HW.30 (`deploy/zephyr-admin-node/HARDWARE_VERDICT.md` @ `## The transmit pool image: steps HW.26 to HW.30`): the pool sat at 0x2800c860 to 0x2800f860 inside the non-cacheable section, 43 frames left from slots read in place by the controller, every slot came home (free 8 of 8, started equal to completed), and the capture held 43 of 43 datagrams from the node with valid IPv4 and UDP checksums; the last in-place descriptor began 2 bytes past a word boundary inside a slot and the frame came out right. RECEIVE, HW.31 to HW.35 (`deploy/zephyr-admin-node/HARDWARE_VERDICT.md` @ `## The receive pool image: steps HW.31 to HW.35`): the pool sat at 0x28009860 to 0x2800f860, the controller wrote 49 frames into slots lwIP took lent with none copied, the session read 36 datagrams in place with none copied, every slot came home (refused 0), and the session's stack peaked at 20352 of 32768 bytes. Both board-table rows are graded HARDWARE (`deploy/zephyr-boards.json` @ `"verdict": "HW.31 to HW.35 held on the receive pool image with the launcher, each step ending OK"`), so no frame was read out of a slot by the controller on the strength of a model alone.
NOT MEASURED, stated as measurements not taken and not as work left unbuilt: a start after the board's power was removed completely, a pool run dry under load (the counts end at nothing refused with one router session as the only load), a datagram that needed IP fragmentation, the Windows and macOS platform legs, which do not build this feature, and the hosted verdict of the push that carries this paragraph. The 2 MiB test-stack overflow of two dissect and passive tests under --all-features, and a large-budget batch window on the AP stream driver, which lends a buffer of the whole negotiated batch that the four spare buffers do not keep, were carried by R3238 and are not this atom's grade.

scouting-responder.reason: COMPLETE: the ANSWERING half of multicast scouting -- recv a Scout on the group, reply with this node's Hello UNICAST to the asker. Gated scouting-responder (wz-runtime-tokio::scouting_responder over wz-session-core::scout_responder); NOT implied by scouting-active, which is the asking half. Distinct from scouting-passive: that atom is wz's periodic re-scout mode (Cooldown, still an initiator, deferred), this is being FINDABLE, which upstream has on by default. Witness: zenohd_scouts_wz_interop -- a stock zenohd told nothing finds wz and dials it. RESIDUAL vs zenoh 1.5.0: upstream picks the reply's SOURCE socket by longest-octet-match against the asker's address over every unicast socket (orchestrator.rs:1113-1134 get_best_match), so on a multi-homed host the Hello leaves the interface nearest the asker; wz answers from the group socket it received on, which is one interface's choice made at bind. CORRECTION (Round 2219) -- THE NAMED RESIDUAL IS CLOSED and the grade moves PARTIAL -> COMPLETE. wz now elects the reply's SOURCE the way upstream does: wz_session_core::scout_responder::best_reply_source is the pure rule (longest shared octet prefix, with upstream's max_by tie-break kept so an identical candidate list in an identical order elects the identical socket), ScoutingResponder::with_reply_sockets holds the unicast sockets and drops any whose local_addr cannot be read (upstream's own filter at orchestrator.rs:1130), UdpDriver::bind_reply_unicast binds each on a CONCRETE address with no link peer, and link_interfaces::multicast_interface_addresses derives the population the way get_interfaces("auto") does (UP + RUNNING + IFF_MULTICAST, first IPv4 per interface) -- resolved LIVE per call rather than out of upstream's process-lifetime lazy_static snapshot, and returning None for "could not determine" where upstream returns the same empty vec it uses for "no interface qualifies". wz-ap-demo --scout-listen binds them from --scout-iface's own addresses or from that enumeration, so the capability is reached by the product and not only by a test. ONE DIVERGENCE, in wz's favour and pinned by a test: a candidate of a different address family scores nothing here, where upstream's zip truncates a v4 asker against a v6 socket's first four octets and can elect a socket that cannot carry the reply at all. WHICH SOCKET ANSWERED IS NOW REPORTED (ResponderStep::Answered.from, ReplySource::Elected|Group), so a node with no unicast socket is a named arm a reader can see rather than a default that looks like a choice. WITNESSES: 5 unit tests in wz-session-core -- the multi-homed election plus its different-asker CONTROL, prefix-beats-position from both ends of the list, the upstream tie rule, the cross-family trap, and the empty list -- and a socket-level Layer M leg in which two askers on 127.0.0.1 and 127.0.0.2 reach one responder and each Hello leaves the address nearest its asker, asserted BOTH from the responder's own report and from what the asker's recv_from sees; the lane's count guard moves 2 -> 3. RED-FIRST: a constant election reds 4 units and the leg; a responder that ignores the election reds the leg on its ReplySource::Group arm; upstream's cross-family zip reds the trap test. THE COMPLETE CLAIM WAS RE-VERIFIED ADVERSARIALLY against the whole of Runtime::responder (zenoh orchestrator.rs:1112-1191) rather than against the residual sentence alone, and the two remaining differences were MEASURED rather than assumed: (1) the self-echo gate is wz's ZID compare where upstream compares the datagram source against its own ucast socket addresses -- already argued in scout_responder.rs gate 3, and not a capability gap, since upstream's form cannot see a co-located second wz process and the ZID compare can; (2) upstream re-reads get_locators() per Hello where wz builds ResponderIdentity once -- VACUOUS in this tree, because upstream's refresh exists to serve spawn_add_listener (orchestrator.rs:544-553) and wz has no runtime listener-add path at all, so nothing can change the advertised set after the responder starts. Upstream's multicast-TTL call on these sockets (orchestrator.rs:746) is likewise not mirrored and is not a gap: it is load-bearing there only because upstream sends its own Scouts from the same sockets it answers from, and wz's asking half sends from bind_multicast_tx_v4, which does set it. PIN RE-DECLARED (R2401). The grade HOLDS: the source-election rule Round 2219 ported is still upstream's at the pin, read rather than assumed (`zenoh/src/net/runtime/orchestrator.rs` @ `fn get_best_match`) -- longest shared octet prefix, computed by zipping the octets and taking the first inequality, with the same `max_by` tie-break that makes an identical candidate list in an identical order elect the identical socket. BUT ONE MECHANISM CLAUSE HAS ROTTED UNDER A CONCLUSION THAT HOLDS, which is the same shape as a dead path and is recorded rather than quietly dropped. This reason says wz drops a socket "whose local_addr cannot be read", calling that upstream's own filter. At the pin there is no such filter at election time: the socket type carries its interface address as an EAGER field, documented as the one used for multicast egress and responder matching, so the fallibility now lives at construction and the election iterates a set that already has an interface. The wz behaviour is unchanged and still correct -- a socket whose address cannot be determined is not a candidate either way -- but the JUSTIFICATION "upstream filters here too" no longer describes the pin, and the line number this reason gave for that filter has rotted with it. WHAT THAT DOES NOT CHANGE: upstream still `unwrap()`s the election result at its one call site, so it assumes a non-empty candidate set, and wz returning None for "could not determine" remains the divergence in wz's favour that this reason already records.

session-close-ingress.source: R2676 register item 761 — session lifetime verb over the shared ingress
session-close-ingress.reason: PARTIAL: F=a rail message closes a RUNNING session -- the session FSM's `session.close` reachable from outside the process through the one ingress port AP and MCU share. P=no upstream counterpart: zenoh's admin write plane carries no close verb, and its handler could not answer one if it did -- it is a Push primitive at `zenoh/src/net/runtime/adminspace.rs` @ `fn send_push_consume(` with no response channel at all, which is why this verb has no reply and success is observable only as the effect. Catalog precedent for a capability upstream lacks: `switchboard`, `ext-pubsub-group-membership`, `locator-iface`. C=wz opens and closes over the rail; opening already worked (`connect-add` reconciles to a dial and InitSyn leaves, witness `wz_router_hat_connect_reconcile.rs`) and closing now does too. BUILT R2678, and the base it fixes is the reason it took a round to find: THE KEYEXPR MATCHER AND THE FSM ENGINE ARE IN TWO OWNERSHIP DOMAINS THAT WERE NEVER IN SCOPE TOGETHER. The matcher runs under the observer lock on the `Session` handle, whose `SessionInner` does not hold the engine; the engine is owned by `OpenedSession`, moved into `drive_session_until_terminal` and borrowed `&mut` there for its whole life. So the seam is a take-once REQUEST that crosses between them as data: `SessionCore::requested_close` on the shared bundle, `SessionLinkActions::request_close` / `take_requested_close` (the shape `take_pending_batch` already established), and `drive::check_requested_close`, which raises `SessionFsmUnicastEvent::SessionClose` on the engine it is handed -- the peer of `check_lease_deadline`, the only other production raiser in the tree, beside it in the same file and generic over `R: SessionRuntime` for the same reason. THE HOOK WAS DELIBERATELY NOT WIDENED: the drive loop calls `on_event(IterationEvent)` while holding the engine, so lending it there was the obvious move and is wrong -- that hook is the application observer fan, and handing every app callback `&mut` on the session's state machine is authority the hook has no business granting. The request travels; the authority stays. INGRESS: `drive::SessionLifecycleInjector` implements the unconditional `EventInjector` port, so the keyexpr table, the matcher and the port are the ones both profiles already share; it is the first injector in the tree that does not wrap an SCE `Engine`. It carries NO literal event name -- it asks the generated machine through `StatePolicy::get_event_from_name`, because a name agreed by hand between two places stays agreed only until one is edited, which is open-debt item 777's whole subject. AP/MCU PARITY IS STRUCTURAL, NOT CLAIMED: every piece above is in `wz-session-core`, which both runtimes build, and both forward the feature; nothing was added to the AP-only admin plane, which is `#[cfg(feature = "adminspace-core")]` and alloc-based and which no MCU crate references. WITNESS `crates/wz-runtime-tokio/tests/session_close_ingress.rs`: a row is registered, a wire Push arrives on it, the ingress stages, the comparator drains, and the assertion is the STATE -- Established to Closing -- because an assertion on the request alone would pass with the raiser deleted. It asserts the ingress did NOT move the machine (it has no engine), that the drain is take-once, and it carries an anti-vacuity arm on an unmapped keyexpr plus a pin that the registered name is the one the document declares. RESIDUAL, stated rather than hidden: no production host registers a row yet -- the capability is reachable and witnessed end to end, but which keyexpr a deployment exposes it on is a deployment's choice and wz ships no default row, so a node does not answer this verb until its host maps one. AND A LANE RUNS THAT WITNESS, which is a separate sentence from "the witness exists" and the one this grade actually needs: both features are non-default, so the changed-crate push gate compiles the file to NOTHING and no hosted lane turned either on -- the tests would have passed by hand and been executed by nothing, a green over a population of zero. R2678 adds the `wz-runtime-tokio|hook|session-close-ingress,switchboard|session_close_ingress` row to `scripts/lib/nondefault-tests-gate.sh`, so the hook runs them on every push and Layer C1bn runs them hosted. Every test in the file carries the atom's name as a prefix so a test added later is covered without touching that row. REGRADE (Round 2697, owner instruction 2026-09-17, sequencing ruled 2026-09-18): THIS ATOM IS PARTIAL AGAIN, AND THE NUMBER WENT UP. Nothing above was withdrawn -- the machine Round 2678 built still stands and its witnesses still pass. What changed is the SCOPE: the owner's interface decision (open-debt item 761, taken 2026-09-17 under "ignore the cost, be right for the long run") settles three things this grade was never given for, so the honest move is to lower the grade rather than let a COMPLETE keep asserting a scope it does not cover. THE THREE RESIDUALS, in the order the item fixes as the order of work: (a) ACL FIRST -- a lifecycle verb sits behind access control, and the measurement behind that ordering is that `wz-session-core/src/switchboard.rs`, `wz-session-core/src/observer.rs` and `wz-runtime-tokio/src/observer.rs` carry ZERO ACL references while `access-acl` is itself PARTIAL; a destructive verb shipped without its gate cannot be recalled, and adding the gate after a harness starts speaking the verb breaks the harness. Acceptance: a refused command changes nothing, and the refusal is observed as nothing happening, because this port answers nothing by design. (b) ONE DECLARATION -- a second binding kind (`lifecycle:`) in `wz-switchboard.yaml`, so the AP registry and the MCU's generated static match take their row from the SAME document. Today each host wires its own keyexpr by hand, which is the defect class this feature's own comment cites (item 777: a hand-agreed string is agreed only until one side is edited). Acceptance: no host binds a row by hand -- one declaration, two profiles. (c) `open` ON THE SAME DOOR -- the same port and the same grammar, `@/<zid>/<whatami>/session/<verb>/<peer-zid>`, with `connect-add` kept as the AP alias. Teaching a second implementation ONE mechanism is the point. Acceptance: both verbs stand on one grammar. WHY THE KEYEXPR CARRIES THE TARGET rather than the payload: ACL filters by keyexpr, so a target in the payload makes "may close session X only" INEXPRESSIBLE -- the decision is about what can be authorised, not about encoding. WHY `session/` AND NOT `config/`: this is a command, and a config sub-key carries the implication that writing the same value twice is harmless. THE COUNT: REMAINING WORK goes 27 -> 28 with this entry, and that rise is the price of the grade telling the truth. It is recorded here rather than absorbed, and this round deliberately closes no atom, so the two movements are never netted against each other. CORRECTION (R2713, residual (a)): THE LIFECYCLE VERB NOW SITS BEHIND AN AUTHORITY, AND TWO HALVES OF CLAUSE (a) WERE REFUTED BEFORE IT WAS BUILT. Re-measured, one command each: `access-acl` is COMPLETE, not PARTIAL as clause (a) states; and the "ZERO ACL references" half survives only after correcting the instrument -- the six `acl` hits in `switchboard.rs` are Anti-Corruption Layer, not access control, and by access-control identifiers (`access_control|AccessControl|Permission|authoris`) `wz-session-core/src/switchboard.rs`, `wz-session-core/src/observer.rs` and `wz-runtime-tokio/src/observer.rs` read 0, 0, 0. WHERE THE GATE HAD TO GO, forced rather than chosen: `wz-access-control` DEPENDS ON `wz-session-core` (it reads `keyexpr_includes_target` and `link::LinkSubject` from it), so the shared port cannot call the policy kernel without a cycle; and the enforcement that does carry the face context, `Session::apply_acl_ingress`, lives in `wz-runtime-tokio`, which no MCU crate builds -- a gate there would withdraw the AP/MCU parity this reason asserts above. Dependency inversion is the only shape that leaves the gate where both profiles build it. WHAT WAS BUILT: `drive::SessionCloseAuthority`, judged on the KEYEXPR because that is where the grammar puts the target, and taken by `SessionLifecycleInjector::new` as a CONSTRUCTOR parameter -- so a host that wires this ingress cannot reach the verb without having answered who may use it, the move the ACL kernel made for `Option<&Zid>` one layer out. The switchboard gains a third row kind, `SwitchboardRowKind::Command`, dispatched through a new defaulted `EventInjector::inject_command(name, keyexpr)`: the value shape needed the payload, a command needs the key, and the registry stays policy-free because it routes by kind and asks nothing. THE DEFAULT IS THE SAFE DIRECTION IN BOTH NEW PLACES -- the trait method defaults to `false`, and this injector's SIGNAL shape no longer closes at all. That second one names the defect exactly: R2678 closed the session from the name-only path, so the verb was reachable by a caller that could not know which session it named and therefore could not ask. WITNESS, in the file the lane row already covers by prefix: `session_close_ingress_refuses_a_close_the_authority_denies` is THE JOIN both ends lacked (a policy drops a governed message from a batch; a matched row closes a running session; neither said the verb was GOVERNED); `..._cannot_be_reached_through_the_signal_path` asserts the row MATCHED (count 1) and nothing closed, so the count cannot stand in for the claim; `..._judges_the_arriving_keyexpr_not_the_row` runs ONE wildcard row and two keys past an authority admitting one, so neither the pattern nor the event name can be what decided. CONTROLS: restoring the signal-path close reds exactly the fail-closed arm (6 passed, 1 failed); consulting the authority and discarding its verdict reds exactly the two refusal arms (5 passed, 2 failed) -- the compile-time shape of that control was rejected first, because a dead-field error is not the behaviour a regression would have. STILL PARTIAL AND THE GRADE DOES NOT MOVE: residual (b), one `lifecycle:` declaration, and residual (c), `open` on the same door, are untouched, and the MCU generated static `match` emits no command row yet -- which is (b)'s subject rather than a second gate. CORRECTION (R2714, residual (b), AP HALF): THE DOCUMENT CAN NOW DECLARE THE ROW, AND ON AP IT REACHES THE EFFECT. Residual (b) asked for one declaration serving two profiles; this lands the declaration and the AP renderer, and the MCU renderer is named below as what remains. MEASURED FIRST, and it found TWO absences rather than the one the clause implies. (1) The sidecar could not express the row at all: `SwitchboardSpec` derived a row's kind from `Binding::codec` PRESENCE, a two-valued discriminator with no third state, and its unit is ONE machine cross-checked against that machine's `external_ingress_events` -- while a close verb belongs to the session FSM, which every profile has and no sidecar names. (2) There was NO AP renderer at all: `grep -rln SwitchboardSpec --include=*.rs crates/` returned exactly two files, the schema and the MCU generator. `wz-switchboard-example` populated a registry with three literal `register*` calls under a comment reading "in production the AP loader fills this by parsing the runtime sidecar" -- and no such loader existed. A comment is not a seam, and that one had been asserting a component into being. WHAT WAS BUILT: `SwitchboardSpec::lifecycle`, a SECOND SECTION rather than a third flavour of `Binding`, because what differs is not the payload shape but WHICH MACHINE the row targets; `LifecycleBinding` carries keyexpr + event and no `codec` field exists on it, so a codec on a lifecycle row is unrepresentable rather than forbidden by a rule. `SwitchboardRegistry::apply_spec` is the mapping, and it lives on the REGISTRY beside `register` / `register_value` / `register_command` deliberately: the defect is hosts writing their own rows, so the cure sits where a host is already looking. A lifecycle row maps to `register_command`, never `register` -- the signal shape carries no keyexpr, so R2713's fail-closed rule would refuse such a row forever. The DESERIALIZE stays at each consumer's I/O boundary, which is the schema crate's own contract and is why the mapping stays `no_std` and the model still pulls no format backend. ⛔ THE MCU GENERATOR REFUSES THE SECTION RATHER THAN DROPPING IT (`CodegenError::LifecycleUnsupported`, checked before any arm is emitted). Skipping it would compile a document declaring a close row into a dispatch that never answers the verb -- a node silent about a capability its own sidecar declares, which is indistinguishable from the capability being absent. A build that would produce that silence now stops. WITNESS: `apply_spec_maps_each_section_to_its_row_kind` asserts the SHAPE each row dispatched through, not the count, because a lifecycle row mis-mapped to `register` still matches and still counts; `session_close_ingress_closes_from_a_switchboard_document` drives a model through the registry to a CLOSED session with no hand registration anywhere in it; `a_documented_row_is_still_refused_by_the_authority` pins that declaring a key is not permitting it, and asserts the row registered before asserting the refusal, so it cannot pass for the opposite of its reason. CONTROLS: mapping a lifecycle row to `register` reds exactly one arm (15 passed, 1 failed); dropping the lifecycle section from `apply_spec` reds exactly the two document arms (7 passed, 2 failed) -- the first spelling of that control redded only ONE of them, which is what exposed the vacuity now closed. Gate 8 also earned its keep here: widening `SwitchboardSpec` broke the schema crate's own initializers and the workspace check named them. STILL PARTIAL. What remains of (b) is the MCU renderer: the generated static `match` emits no command arm, so a lifecycle row is an AP-only capability today and the refusal above is what keeps that honest rather than silent. Residual (c), `open` on the same door, is untouched. CORRECTION (R2716, residual (b), MCU HALF): THE GENERATOR EMITS THE LIFECYCLE ARM, SO ONE DOCUMENT NOW SERVES BOTH PROFILES. R2714's `CodegenError::LifecycleUnsupported` is replaced by `LifecycleFactsMissing`, which is the same refusal with a narrower reason -- a section is still never DROPPED. WHY IT WAS NOT ONE MORE MATCH ARM, measured before building: a sidecar is a ONE-MACHINE document (`SwitchboardSpec::machine`, cross-checked by the generator against that machine's `external_ingress_events`), and a lifecycle verb belongs to the session FSM, which every profile has and no sidecar names. Judging a lifecycle row against the application machine would reject every correct row, because `session.close` is not a thermostat event. So the generator needed a SECOND machine's facts, not a second branch. WHAT WAS BUILT: `GenInput::session_facts: Option<&MachineFacts>` -- an Option because a document declaring no lifecycle row should not have to compile a machine it does not use, and a document that DOES declare one and supplies `None` is refused before a single binding arm is written.
