F=the SHM establishment handshake; P=zenoh `init::ext::Shm` (`zextzbuf!(0x2)`) + `open::ext::Shm` (`zextz64!(0x2)`), FSM at `establishment/ext/shm.rs`; C=requires transport-shm. wz now runs zenoh's real CHALLENGE-RESPONSE, not the scoped UNIT capability offer/reflect/`&=` the prior reason recorded as the substitute. The exchange: InitSyn carries the initiator's AUTH SEGMENT id; the acceptor MAPS that segment, reads the random challenge inside it, and returns it on InitAck beside its own segment id; the initiator validates the echo against its own challenge, maps the acceptor's segment, and answers with ITS challenge on OpenSyn; the acceptor validates that second echo and confirms with the literal 1 on OpenAck. Each side therefore PROVES map-ability to the other -- a token exchange would pass between two hosts that share nothing. The segment is a real POSIX object (`wz-runtime-tokio::shm_auth_segment`, `/dev/shm/{id}.zenoh` -- the NAME is wire format, since a foreign peer opens exactly that string) holding a u64 array `[protocols.len(), !challenge, SHM_VERSION, POSIX_PROTOCOL_ID]`; the challenge is stored BITWISE-INVERTED as upstream stores it, which is load-bearing interop rather than obfuscation. `SHM_VERSION` mismatch, an unmappable segment, and a wrong echo all degrade to "no shared memory" with the session intact; only a MALFORMED InitSyn body aborts, mirroring zenoh's one `bail!` and its asymmetry with the initiator's tolerant `recv_init_ack`. OPT-IN: the dispatch is EMPTY until an authenticator is installed, and an empty one emits nothing, so a deploy that installs none keeps the pre-R311y507 UNIT wire byte-identical; the two mechanisms never half-mix, because the challenge REPLACES the UNIT ext at the stage seam and the offer predicate follows whichever mechanism is running. CROSS-IMPL PROVEN (A4, `wz_shm_establishment_zenohd_interop`, run-ci Layer Z) against a real `zenohd --features shared-memory`: BOTH directions now report `shm negotiated = true` where R311y505 correctly asserted `false` for the UNIT mechanism. DAMAGE-BOUND: storing the challenge un-inverted flips both legs to `false` with the session still Established, so the green is bound to the exact page layout zenohd reads; a second damage (accepting any echo) reds the forged-challenge unit test while leaving the wz<->wz e2e green, which is the honest split -- two cooperating wz peers cannot show that the CHECK is enforced. Still scoped vs upstream: no segment pool / watchdog / generation, and wz never takes the EXCLUSIVE flock upstream uses to invalidate a recycled segment (wz has no pool for it to guard). The TX side was already there (Session::publish_shm reads is_shm() and swaps the descriptor for the bytes); the RX un-swap honoured the 0x2 body marker ALONE, so an un-negotiated peer could still make this node map a segment it named. The gate now lives on the data path where it belongs -- see the transport-shm atom for the mechanism, the zenoh citation and the damage-bound proof. A live listener holds the lock, so a second bind is refused with AddrInUse instead of pulling the socket out from under it; a CRASHED one released it when its fd closed, so its leftovers are still reclaimed. The bind returns a new owning type, UnixsockListener (crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/unixsock_pipeline.rs), and BoundListener::Unixsock carries THAT instead of a bare UnixListener -- so the production bind_locator seam is arbitrated, not only the primitive the e2e harness calls. UnixsockListener::close is the del_listener counterpart (`io/zenoh-links/zenoh-link-unixsock_stream/src/unicast.rs` @ `async fn del_listener`): unlock, close the fd, unlink the socket file. Drop runs the same teardown, which is STRONGER than upstream's registry-only lifecycle -- an early return or a panic no longer leaks a socket file. The lock is the same raw libc::flock this crate already makes for the unixpipe rendezvous and the SHM auth segment, i.e. the same BSD lock upstream's nix::fcntl::flock takes, so the arbitration is cross-IMPLEMENTATION by construction rather than merely cross-wz.

The unit zenohs_lock_file_unlink_reopens_the_stale_window runs BOTH orders over ONE helper and MEASURES two holders under upstream's order against one under wz's, so this is a control group rather than a claim. The cost is one zero-byte 0600 file per bound path, and it is invisible to upstream, which opens its lock file O_CREAT.

Dropping the flock reds {a_live_listener_keeps_its_socket_against_a_second_bind, every_path_addressed_bind_seam_takes_an_advisory_lock} and leaves close_and_drop_both_release_the_path GREEN, because the lock FILE is still created; dropping the teardown unlink reds close_and_drop_both_release_the_path at its socket assertion; adopting upstream's lock-file unlink reds the SAME test at its lock-file assertion. THE CONTROL: the same publisher against a wz acceptor that does not offer SHM delivers three raw samples byte-exact, so the zero is about shared memory and not about the topology, the declarations or the harness. wz to zenoh: `z_sub_shm` listens, wz dials, negotiates and calls `publish_shm`; zenoh's RX task fails with `decoding error` (`io/zenoh-transport/src/unicast/universal/rx.rs` @ `.map_err(|_| zerror!("{}: decoding error", link.link))?;`) and CLOSES THE TRANSPORT.

WHY. With the Put's `ext_shm` marker set, zenoh lays the payload out SLICED (`commons/zenoh-codec/src/zenoh/put.rs` @ `let codec = Zenoh080Sliced::<u32>::new(ext_shm.is_some());`): a count of slices, then per slice a kind byte (RAW 0, SHM_PTR 1) and a length-prefixed body, which for SHM_PTR is the encoded `ShmBufInfo` (`commons/zenoh-codec/src/core/zbuf.rs` @ `impl<W> WCodec<&ZBuf, &mut W> for Zenoh080Sliced<$bound>`). wz writes and reads a single length and the four descriptor varints (`crates/wz-session-core/src/push_build.rs` @ `let payload_len = descriptor_bytes.len() as u64;`). That is self-consistent, so every wz-to-wz test is green and no symmetric fixture can see it. The layout needs the Put codec to branch on a preceding TLV-chain entry, which SCE's `sce:present-if` cannot express: open-debt item 823, reported to SCE on 2026-09-26 and re-measured against SCE's HEAD on 2026-10-01, where it is still refused. A hand-written Put decoder is the wrong repair, because it breaks the codec SSOT, so nothing is built on top of one.

WHAT THIS CHANGES IN THE RESIDUAL. The order of what can be measured is the layout first (SCE), then, ON TOP OF IT, the lifecycle this reason names, and the same harness already shows which is the next red. `ShmBackedPayload` invalidates its slot and unlinks its segment the moment its owner lets go; zenoh's sender holds the buffer by a reference count it takes on every serialization (`commons/zenoh-codec/src/core/zbuf.rs` @ `unsafe { shmb.inc_ref_count() };`) and the receiver's `Drop` releases it. THE NAMED RESIDUAL "the receiver takes no refcount" IS REFUTED as a divergence: a read does not increment it upstream either (`commons/zenoh-shm/src/reader.rs` @ `// Read does not increment the reference count as it is assumed`). What a receiver owes is the decrement on drop and the watchdog confirmation (`commons/zenoh-shm/src/watchdog/confirmator.rs` @ `pub static mut GLOBAL_CONFIRMATOR: WatchdogConfirmator =`, every 50 ms), and what invalidates a buffer no holder confirmed is the provider's validator, every 100 ms. The atom `api-compat-c` is blocked by the same item, through its SHM half and the two symbols behind it.

UPDATE (R3038) -- THE PROVIDER'S LIFECYCLE ARM IS BUILT: A CHUNK NOW LIVES BY UPSTREAM'S REFERENCE COUNT, AND THE ARM THAT WAS A PIN IS THE POSITIVE WITNESS. THE ATOM STAYS PARTIAL ON WHAT IS STILL OPEN. THE DEFECT, AND A SECOND ONE FOUND ON THE WAY. wz's provider invalidated a slot and unlinked its data segment when its owner let go (open-debt item 823 (6)), so a publisher that dropped its payload as `publish_shm` returned left a zenoh reader nothing to open. The second defect was on the receiving side and nothing had measured it: a descriptor is sent with one reference taken for its receiver, and wz's resolver read the chunk and never gave that reference back, so a sustained zenoh shared-memory stream into a wz subscriber would have kept every chunk out of the publisher's pool. MEASURED, with the resolver's release removed, which is what the old resolver did: all three chunks a `z_pub_shm` handed over still read a count of one in zenoh's own metadata segment after wz had read them. THE PROTOCOL, taken from upstream and stated once in the provider's module docs: the count starts at 1 as the owner's own reference; serializing a descriptor takes one more for the receiver (`commons/zenoh-codec/src/core/zbuf.rs` @ `unsafe { shmb.inc_ref_count() };`) and a read takes none; every holder gives its reference back when it lets go (`commons/zenoh-shm/src/lib.rs` @ `impl Drop for ShmBufInner {`); the provider collects a chunk when the count reads zero (`commons/zenoh-shm/src/api/provider/shm_provider.rs` @ `fn garbage_collect_impl<const SAFE: bool>(&self) -> usize {`) and a reclaimed slot advances its generation, which turns every descriptor of it stale (`commons/zenoh-shm/src/metadata/storage.rs` @ `pub fn reclaim(`). WHAT WAS BUILT. Serializing the descriptor is one guarded step: (`crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/shm_provider.rs` @ `pub fn wire_reference(&self) -> WireReference<'_> {`) takes the reference and returns it if the frame does not build or the send refuses. The resolver gives back the one reference exactly once on every way out once the header's generation shows it is its own, saturating at zero so a replayed descriptor cannot wrap the count; a header of another generation is another buffer's and is not touched, which upstream's reader would decrement. The owner's drop gives back its own reference and parks the data segment, mapped and locked, on a busy list, because upstream's orphan cleanup deletes any segment nobody holds a shared lock on; the list is collected when an owner drops and when a payload is allocated (`crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/shm_provider.rs` @ `fn collect_garbage(&mut self) -> usize {`), slots go to the back of a first-in first-out queue as upstream's do, and the generation advances at reclaim and not at allocation. The receiver maps the provider's metadata segment WRITABLE, which releasing a reference needs; the first build mapped it read-only and died with a SIGSEGV on the first release. A resolver is now offered EVERY shared-memory slice of a message, not only those before the first fault, because a slice it never sees is a reference nobody releases (`crates/wz-session-core/src/put_payload.rs` @ `fn every_shm_slice_reaches_the_resolver_after_one_fails() {`). WITNESSED, in both directions and off the OTHER side's bookkeeping. Against upstream's own programs, the zenoh-to-wz leg reads zenoh's metadata segment after wz has read each sample and asserts every chunk was given back; the two wz-to-zenoh legs assert the chunk comes home to wz's provider after zenoh's subscriber lets go, a decrement made by zenoh's own drop in a process wz does not control; and the leg for a publisher that lets go at once is the positive twin of the held leg (`crates/wz-integration-tests/tests/wz_shm_payload_zenohd_interop.rs` @ `async fn wz_shm_payload_its_owner_let_go_of_at_once_is_still_readable_by_a_zenohd_shm_subscriber() {`), where it was a pin of the defect. In-process, twelve provider tests, among them the arm that leaves a chunk standing for a receiver after its owner has gone (`crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/shm_provider.rs` @ `fn an_owner_that_lets_go_leaves_its_chunk_standing_for_the_receiver_that_holds_it() {`). Four mutations, each restored byte for byte: the receiver without its release reds the zenoh-to-wz leg alone, with the count zenoh reports; serializing without the reference reds the let-go leg alone, with the very `Error receiving SHM buffer` the pin used to assert; the owner's drop without its own release reds both wz-to-zenoh legs on the chunk never coming home; the early return in the slice walk reds its test alone. The MCU multicast image does not move (64172 before and after). STILL OPEN, and why the atom stays partial: no WATCHDOG, so a holder that dies without releasing leaves its chunk parked until the process ends and nothing invalidates it; no POOL, one data segment per payload at chunk offset 0; the receiver still copies the bytes off the page before it releases, so a delivered sample is not the segment; a keyexpr that does not resolve returns before the un-swap and so releases nothing; a reference taken for a frame that is then dropped before it leaves is never released, as upstream's is not; and wz as a ROUTER relaying an SHM put is unmeasured against the reference count. NOT MEASURED: the hosted run, because the oracle legs SKIP where the shared-memory source build is absent and the in-process tests are all that hosted CI sees of this; and any host other than this Linux build machine.

UPDATE (R3040) -- THE WATCHDOG, THE RECEIVER'S HOLD AND THE HANDOFF ACKNOWLEDGEMENT ARE BUILT, AND THE WATCHDOG IS WITNESSED AGAINST UPSTREAM'S OWN VALIDATOR. THE ATOM STAYS PARTIAL ON WHAT IS STILL OPEN. THE WATCHDOG (R3039). Upstream's two halves never meet: every holder confirms a chunk's bit, bit slot % 64 of word slot / 64, at once on attaching and every 50 ms while it holds (`commons/zenoh-shm/src/watchdog/confirmator.rs` @ `WatchdogConfirmator::new(Duration::from_millis(50));`), and the provider clears it every 100 ms and marks a chunk invalidated when it finds it clear (`commons/zenoh-shm/src/watchdog/validator.rs` @ `WatchdogValidator::new(Duration::from_millis(100));`). Here a process-wide confirmator (`crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/shm_watchdog.rs` @ `pub(crate) struct Confirmator {`) tracks the bits this process holds, one thread ticks it every 50 ms and every second tick validates what the provider allocated (`crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/shm_provider.rs` @ `fn validate(&mut self) -> usize {`); an owner's handle confirms while it lives, and an invalidated chunk is only MARKED, reclaiming staying with the reference count as upstream's default collection leaves it. A receiver's hold (`crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/shm_provider.rs` @ `pub struct ChunkHold {`) is upstream's received buffer as a lifecycle: it attaches to the watchdog first, takes no reference, stays confirmed while held, gives its reference back on drop and refuses a header of another generation. A receiver keeps a provider's metadata mapping by id and trusts it only while the name still names the same file (`crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/posix_shm.rs` @ `pub fn is_current(&self) -> bool {`). THE DEFECT FOUND ON THE WAY: wz never ACKNOWLEDGED what it received. A zenoh sender that puts a shared-memory buffer on a reliable link parks a hard reference to it, which is a confirmed descriptor (`commons/zenoh-shm/src/lib.rs` @ `pub struct ShmBufHardRef(ConfirmedDescriptor);`), and drops it only when its receiver lowers a counter in the SENDER's auth segment, one counter per priority, at the ids the sender names in its Open message (`io/zenoh-transport/src/unicast/establishment/ext/shm/handoff.rs` @ `pub fn on_rx(&self, priority: Priority) {`). wz decoded that counter block and discarded it. MEASURED, and not inferred: against upstream's own publisher the counter read 1, 2, 3 for three puts and stayed 3 for the rest of the run, and every chunk read confirmed and never invalidated for as long as the process lived, where the same chunks between two zenoh programs are invalidated within about 200 ms. The decisive experiment needed no wz process: upstream's own subscriber frozen with SIGSTOP after the connection came up, so that it could acknowledge nothing as wz did, took the counter to 5 with every chunk at refcount 1, not invalidated and confirmed for about five seconds, and thawing it dropped the counter to nothing and invalidated all six chunks within 400 ms. This is also why the first attempt at a witness for the watchdog could not be kept: its control, a chunk nobody confirms, never became invalid, in three designs, because zenoh itself kept confirming it. THE ACKNOWLEDGEMENT. The Open exchange keeps the peer's segment with its challenge and, once the echo of our challenge checks out, opens a handoff from the counter block the peer named, the initiator's OpenSyn for an acceptor and the acceptor's OpenAck for an initiator; a new establishment withdraws it, so a registry never writes the counters of a peer it has left. The object is (`crates/wz-session-core/src/extshm.rs` @ `pub trait ShmHandoff: Send + Sync {`) and the AP implementation holds the peer's auth segment mapped writable (`crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/shm_auth_segment.rs` @ `pub struct PeerHandoff {`), lowers `counters[ids[band]]` and SATURATES at zero where upstream's wraps, since a wrapped counter would read as four billion and the sender would never let go of anything again. The subscriber registry acknowledges once per shared-memory slice, at the message's QoS priority whether or not the `pubsub-qos` projection is compiled in, whether or not the slice resolves, and after the attempt to read it, which is upstream's order (`crates/wz-session-core/src/pubsub.rs` @ `fn a_shm_slice_is_acknowledged_once_at_its_messages_priority() {`); a session's dispatch hands the registry the handoff once per change (`crates/wz-runtime-tokio/src/session/tests.rs` @ `fn a_session_acknowledges_the_shm_slices_it_receives_through_the_counters_its_peer_named() {`, driven through a real Open exchange and a real slot-backed Put, so it also holds on a host whose oracle legs skip). WITNESSED AGAINST UPSTREAM: with the acknowledgement built the same run reads the counter empty throughout and the chunks invalidated within about 200 ms, leg 1 asserts that zenoh itself invalidated every chunk wz read, and the watchdog leg has its control (`crates/wz-integration-tests/tests/wz_shm_payload_zenohd_interop.rs` @ `async fn zenohd_shm_publisher_chunk_wz_holds_stays_valid_while_one_wz_released_is_invalidated() {`): wz holds the first chunk zenoh's publisher sends and links and releases the others, zenoh's own validator invalidates the released ones and spares the held one for six windows, which is only true if the bit wz confirms is the bit zenoh's validator clears. MUTATIONS, each restored byte for byte: the decrement removed reds leg 1 and leg 5 and no other leg; the registry stamp removed reds the same two and the session test; the acknowledgement lowering the neighbouring band's counter reds four tests on the counters; acknowledging only slices that resolve reds the unresolvable-slice test alone; and wz confirming bit slot + 1 reds leg 5 on its control, which no in-process test can see because the confirm and the validate share one function. The three watchdog mutations of R3039 red their tests alone as well. A race found by the full run: the provider's orphan-sweep test swept the whole of /dev/shm and read another test's segment, in the instant between its creation and its shared lock, as an orphan; the sweep takes a scope now, and the production function keeps its signature. STILL OPEN, and why the atom stays partial: no POOL, one data segment per payload at chunk offset 0; the receiver still copies the bytes off the page before it releases, so a delivered sample is not the segment; an invalidated chunk is not reclaimed, so a holder that dies without releasing keeps its chunk parked until the process ends; a Put whose keyexpr does not resolve returns before the un-swap and so neither releases nor ACKNOWLEDGES its slices, which now pins them at the sender; wz as a router relaying a shared-memory put is unmeasured against both counts; and wz as a SENDER declares no counters, so the buffers it sends rely on the reference count alone. UPDATE (R3044) -- SCE ACCEPTED THE REQUEST FOR THE VALUE OF A QUERY AND THE PIN CARRIES IT; WZ'S OWN DOCUMENT DOES NOT USE IT YET, SO THE VALUE IS STILL PINNED AND NOT CLOSED. The R3042 update above says upstream's own reader IGNORES the length that the shared-memory value extension declares, and that is not what the source says. The reader subtracts the bytes the encoding took from the declared length and fails when that is negative (`commons/zenoh-codec/src/zenoh/mod.rs` @ `header.len.checked_sub(start - end)`), so the length must be at least the encoding's bytes, and it does not use the length to END the body, which a marker before it makes a list of slices that ends itself. The consequence for this tree is the same, since a reader that trusts the length reads past the frame, but the wording was wrong, and it matters for the sender side wz does not yet build: what it writes there has to be at least the encoding's bytes and no more than that is required. SCE took the request in a shape of its own and not the one asked for: a chain can be told, entry by entry, whether the entry before it was a named marker, and an entry codec that takes that as a flag input splits its body on it, with the declared length read as a field and not used to end the body. It also repaired a defect found on the way, a chain whose entry codec takes a flag input compiling in no language at the pin held before.
